 The Reinsurance Accountant II will support Obsidian, Protective’s specialty property and casualty (P&C) business, which operates in the excess and surplus (E&S) insurance market. Obsidian supports specialty P&C insurance programs and provides the carrier infrastructure, oversight, and access to reinsurance capacity needed to operate and grow these programs. 
   
 In this role, you will support the financial and operational administration of Obsidian’s reinsurance programs, with responsibility for reinsurance cessions and settlements, collateral monitoring, account reconciliations, statutory reporting, and the financial administration of reinsurance agreements. 
   
 
 This is an excellent opportunity for an analytical, detail-oriented professional who is interested in the specialty P&C and E&S insurance market and enjoys understanding how contractual terms translate into financial activity. The successful candidate will bring strong problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to independently manage detailed financial processes while building a deeper understanding of reinsurance and specialty insurance. 
 
  Work Arrangement   This is a primarily remote position. Candidates should reside within reasonable driving distance (~2 hours) of Middletown, Connecticut and be available to travel to the Middletown office approximately 3–5 times per year for team meetings and other business needs.   Key Responsibilities   

 Prepare reinsurance cession statements and support related remittances and settlements. 
 Partner with reinsurers and reinsurance brokers to support cessions, settlements, receivables, and payables. 
 Monitor collateral requirements, including letters of credit and related funding requirements. 
 Support the timely collection and payment of reinsurance receivables and payables. 
 Calculate adjustable reinsurance features, including contingent and sliding-scale commissions. 
 Prepare and post general ledger entries and complete balance sheet reconciliations for reinsurance-related accounts. 
 Assist with Schedule F preparation and other statutory and management reporting requirements. 
 Review reinsurance agreements to understand contractual terms and their impact on accounting and operational processes. 
 Support internal and external discussions related to new and renewal reinsurance agreements. 
 Execute established internal controls accurately and in accordance with company policies. 
 Identify opportunities to improve reporting, processes, controls, and the use of financial data. 
 Support additional reinsurance accounting projects and initiatives as needed. 

   Core Competencies (skills, knowledge and abilities):   

 Understanding of accounting principles and their application to insurance or reinsurance transactions. 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work accurately with detailed financial data. 
 Strong Microsoft Excel capabilities, including experience with pivot tables and lookup functions such as XLOOKUP and VLOOKUP. 
 Ability to interpret financial information and understand the accounting implications of contractual terms. 
 High degree of attention to detail and commitment to financial accuracy. 
 Intellectual curiosity and willingness to investigate discrepancies, ask questions, and develop a deeper understanding of underlying business activity. 
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with internal stakeholders and external reinsurance partners. 
 Ability to organize competing priorities, meet deadlines, and work independently in a remote environment. 

   Required Qualifications   

 Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. 
 2+ years of relevant professional experience in accounting, finance, insurance, reinsurance, or insurance brokerage. 
 Experience with general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, financial reporting, or related accounting processes. 
 Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables and lookup functions. 

   Preferred Qualifications   

 Property & Casualty insurance accounting experience. 
 Reinsurance accounting or reinsurance operations experience. 
 Experience supporting program insurance or program accounting.

description:
Headquarters:  United States (Remote)
 

  Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at   grafana.com   and follow us on   LinkedIn   and   X  . 
 We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. 
 You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.   
 
  This is a remote position and we're considering candidates in the US or Canada (residents of Québec are not eligible for this position).  
 
 The Opportunity 
 About our platform 
 Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. We aim to grow this to hundreds of millions per second, and it's critical that as we grow, we improve our performance, increase our reliability, and do it efficiently and securely. 
 The Foundations department owns the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP): the Kubernetes clusters, cloud service provider resources (CSP), hardware, identity, SDLC, security and observability systems that Grafana Labs's application engineers use to build, deploy, and run their workloads. 
 About the Productivity group 
 We're hiring an engineering manager for the Foundations Productivity group, which owns SDLC tooling, application security and observability, of the resources, systems and workloads used to build and run Grafana Labs products. The group enables product development through the provision of performant and feature-rich SDLC tooling, governing the use and configuration of that tooling.  We are responsible for guiding the product teams in application security good practices, reviewing product changes for security compliance and enabling security functions through self-service automation.  We also own and maintain the internal observability platform, using our own products to give visibility into cloud resource cost, usage and sustainability, and vulnerability management. 
 You'll lead one of the squads of platform engineers that comprise the group. 
 We're platform engineers, and our application teams are our users. Our job is to give them leverage: self-service building blocks that take care of the hard parts of infrastructure, so they can focus on what they're building. We treat the platform as a product and value the experience of the people who use it. When a change is well communicated and understood, teams welcome it, and it lands as an improvement that makes the right way the easy way. You'll lead a squad that makes that happen. 
 How we work 
 Foundations is a global team that works asynchronously. The people who own a component or problem make the decisions about it, once stakeholders have had a chance to weigh in. Application teams build and run their own services; we give them a self-service platform to do it on. 
 Every engineer is on-call for the components their squad provides. We plan on-call, tactical work, and time off into every quarter, so roadmap work is roughly half of an engineer's time rather than all of it.

 Hire, manage, and develop a squad of platform engineers, with regular feedback and career conversations that support each person's growth. 
 Own your squad's roadmap and quarterly objectives: help decide what the squad works on, what it defers, and why, across a broad remit where demand always exceeds capacity. 
 Take platform changes from design to fleet-wide adoption: staged rollouts, migration paths, and clear communication, so changes land well for the teams who depend on them. 
 Partner with the other Productivity squads on work that spans them, and with the teams across Foundations and the rest of Engineering whose work depends on yours. 
 Help shape how the group works as a whole, including planning, on-call, and the ownership model between squads.

  Wrike is the most powerful work management platform. Built for teams and organizations looking to collaborate, create, and exceed every day, Wrike brings everyone and all work into a single place to remove complexity, increase productivity, and free people up to focus on their most purposeful work.

  Your Qualifications:    
 
 Strong expertise with Java/JVM, building scalable, high-performance backend systems; open to leveraging other languages when appropriate.

 A strong interest in how complex systems fail and a track record of designing them to recover gracefully.

You’ll collaborate with other senior engineers who value autonomy, deep technical discussions, and rigorous engineering practices. title: Finance Associate
description:
About Pave Bank   Pave Bank is a fully licensed commercial bank, regulated by the National Bank of Georgia. We are reimagining how global businesses access and move capital by bridging the gap between traditional finance and digital assets. Joining Pave Bank means becoming part of a fast-growing institution redefining this convergence. You will have the opportunity to work alongside second-time founders and industry leaders, gain deep exposure to institutional banking and digital assets, and grow within a dynamic and ambitious team.   The Role   We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Finance Associate to join the Group Finance function, reporting directly to the VP, Finance. You will own the Group's core accounting cycle across multiple entities and jurisdictions, from day-to-day transaction processing and payables through to month-end close, entity accounts and Group consolidation.  This role combines operational delivery with ownership. You will run the close, keep the books and schedules audit-ready, coordinate our auditors, and strengthen the processes and controls behind them. We are a small, fast-moving team, so you will also work on new projects and initiatives across the Group.  We want someone who is proactive, adaptable and solutions-focused, who uses technology and AI to work smarter, and who wants to help build a finance function that scales with the business. You will have the opportunity to grow your scope and responsibility as the business grows in size and complexity.   Key Responsibilities    Close, Entity Accounts and Consolidation   
  Own the monthly, quarterly and annual close calendar across Group entities, and deliver it accurately and on time.  
  Own entity-level accounts, including preparing financial statements under local GAAP.  
  Prepare the Group consolidation under IFRS, including intercompany eliminations, FX translation and consolidation adjustments.  
  Maintain the key accounting schedules (accruals, prepayments, fixed assets, intercompany and other balance sheet schedules) to an audit-ready standard.  
  Assess the accounting treatment of new or non-routine transactions and propose the treatment for review.  
   Accounting and Reconciliations   
  Make sure transactions are recorded accurately and on time across Group entities.  
  Own bank, balance sheet and intercompany reconciliations, investigating and resolving differences.  
  Prepare intercompany recharges and keep intercompany balances agreed and settled across the Group.  
  Maintain the chart of accounts, tracking categories, bank feeds and supporting documentation.  
   Accounts Payable and Payments   
  Own the AP cycle end to end: invoice capture, coding, approval routing, payment scheduling and expense claims.  
  Manage vendor onboarding, vendor master data and vendor queries.  
  Prepare and upload payment batches for approval across the Group's banking platforms.  
   Audit, Statutory and Regulatory Reporting   
  Coordinate Group and entity-level audits: prepare PBC (prepared-by-client) lists and supporting schedules, manage auditor requests, and help resolve audit findings.  
  Prepare statutory accounts and support tax, compliance and regulatory financial submissions across Group entities, working with external advisers.  
   Controls, Policies and Process Improvement   
  Maintain and improve finance procedures, SOPs and controls, with clear segregation of duties.  
  Help develop and document accounting policies and the Group close process.  
  Find and put in place improvements to accounting, reconciliation and reporting workflows using automation, AI and data tools.  
  Help evaluate and implement new finance systems as the function grows.  
   Projects     Lead or support finance projects across the Group as priorities change.     About You   
  Around 5–10 years' experience in accounting, audit, financial reporting or finance operations, in practice, in industry, or both.  
  A track record of owning month-end close, reconciliations and financial statements across multiple entities.  
  Strong working knowledge of IFRS, and the ability to work out and apply the right accounting treatment for non-routine transactions.  
  Hands-on experience of consolidation, intercompany accounting and FX translation, ideally in a multi-entity, multi-currency international group.  
  Experience preparing for or supporting external audits and statutory reporting.  
  Hands-on experience with Xero or a similar cloud accounting system, and strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.  
  A good understanding of what makes a strong process, control and system, and a high level of attention to detail.  
  Comfortable using AI and automation tools to work more efficiently.  
  Proactive, adaptable and solutions-focused: you spot problems, suggest fixes and get things done with minimal supervision.  
  Comfortable in a fast-paced, evolving environment, rolling up your sleeves and taking on whatever needs doing.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.   We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.    Own a vertical end-to-end  — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.  
   Shape the technical design with engineering  — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.  
   Make hard trade-offs  across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.  
   Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs  — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.  
   Apply AI where it earns its place  — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.  
   Ship against external gates  — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.  
   Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.   
  What you'll need  
    Product leadership   — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

  Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap   
  Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch   
  Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds   
  AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted   
  Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged  
  Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

  Grow the base:  lift win rates and velocity on six- and seven-figure expansion opportunities, and open more cross-sell conversations with customers who don’t yet use us for their entire revenue lifecycle process.

  Move as One:  You’ll work daily with SEs, Customer Success, RevOps, Product and Marketing, and share credit for the wins. Our sellers own the renewal and the growth, so you’ll help them mobilize the whole company behind each customer. 
  Evidence over Ego:  You’ll inspect pipeline and forecast using real buyer signals, not gut feel, and say so when the data changes your mind. 
  Lead from the Front:  You’ll coach in the work, stay close to key deals without taking them over, and take ownership early, with or without a title that says you should. 
  Make Your Mark:  You’ll shape how we sell the Predictive Revenue System to enterprise buyers, not just run the existing playbook. 
  Customer-Inspired:  You’ll turn what customers tell you into what we build and say, including why they choose to build, buy or consolidate.

You’re as comfortable inspecting a forecast as you are coaching a hard conversation. If you want to learn more, do more, and become more, this is your next move.

 Our team is committed to enhancing physician and patient quality of life through Elation, a SaaS cloud-based clinical platform. We’ve built a product that users love, and we plan to keep it that way by continuing to empathize with users and help them overcome their most significant challenges. Designing at Elation is humbling, challenging, and rewarding. Our users do work that affects human lives, and our tools can make or break that work. 
  The Role  
 As a Senior/Staff Product Designer, you'll lead the design for how primary care clinicians work. You’ll develop a deep understanding of their workflows to inspire an AI-native experience while keeping the team grounded in day-to-day clinical practice. 
 This role is for someone who creates and champions compelling UX strategy and experience visions while guiding work across multiple squads. You'll shape interaction patterns and contribute to visual language development — all while modeling the craft, curiosity, and collaborative ways of working that raise the bar for designers around you. 
 Clinicians have repeatedly awarded Elation "Best in KLAS" in our category, a recognition that reflects our clinician-first approach to everything we build. Reporting up through our Chief Product Officer, you'll work autonomously within your team while remaining connected to a centralized design group that is deeply collaborative and curious. You'll also find enthusiastic partners in our on-staff physicians, our users, and teams across the organization. 
 If you want to do complex, meaningful work at the place where design and healthcare intersect, we'd love to hear from you! 
  What You'll Do (Role and Responsibilities)  
 
 Deeply understand our users — their problems, workflows, and jobs-to-be-done — to ensure we are always solving for the right thing. 
 Own and lead the design process from discovery to delivery, making key decisions on solution direction and details.

 Collaborate cross-functionally to deliver a clear, consistent, and high-quality user experience.

 Be a leader on the design team by mentoring other designers, leading design critiques, and driving initiatives that improve our culture, tools, and processes.

 8+ years of experience designing and shipping complex, web-based products in a cross-functional team. 
 A strong portfolio demonstrating your ability to navigate ambiguous problem spaces, from research and strategy through to polished, human-centered user experiences. Your portfolio should showcase your strengths in UX, UI, and visual design.

 Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with a track record of building strong partnerships with Product and Engineering.
